attempted_claim: Let A be separable, unital, simple, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, quasidiagonal with finite nuclear dimension and T(A) nonempty. Without assuming the UCT for A, is every tau in T(A) quasidiagonal in Brown's sense — i.e. for every finite F in A and epsilon>0 there are k and c.p.c. psi:A->M_k with ||psi(ab)-psi(a)psi(b)||<epsilon and |tau(a)-tr_k(psi(a))|<epsilon for all a,b in F (equivalently, is there a unital *-homomorphism theta:A->Q_omega with tau_{Q_omega} circ theta = tau)? In particular, does finite nuclear dimension replace the UCT hypothesis in Theorem A of Tikuisis-White-Winter for this class?
decisive_failure: Target work used the published TWW proof and Winter survey via full-text evidence to isolate the single UCT use, plus standard CETWW regularity facts and one bounded monotracial recovery computation. It does not resolve the target in either direction: no UCT-free uniform stable uniqueness theorem was proved and no counterexample was constructed, and the adjacent monotracial fact is folklore rather than an auditable original contribution.
